steps.title: Bright and saline
steps.body: Albariño gives crisp whites with lemon, grapefruit, white peach, apricot, white flowers and a saline, mineral edge. Acidity is high, body light to medium. It's aromatic yet dry. Its home is the Atlantic coast of north-west Spain and northern Portugal.

steps.title: Thick skins
steps.body: Albariño has small berries with thick skins, which resist mildew and rot in its wet, humid homeland. Thick skins also hold aromatic compounds, giving its perfume, and can add a slightly bitter, phenolic finish. Some producers use skin contact or lees ageing for extra texture.
steps.highlight: Thick skins for a wet climate

steps.prompt: Why does Albariño suit its wet, Atlantic home?
options: Its thick skins resist mildew and rot

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon colour, peach and citrus aromas, and a crisp, saline, mineral palate. Compared with Sauvignon Blanc, it's more stone fruit and less green; compared with Viognier, lighter and much fresher.

steps.prompt: Albariño has thin skins that make it prone to rot.
steps.explanation: Not true. Its thick skins help it resist rot.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Albariño gives peach, citrus and a saline edge
Thick skins resist rot in a wet climate
